<!-- name: Look Up -->
<!-- board: Real drones detected, at last | Flock-You's Flock signatures | 18 more time zones -->
**Look Up.** Squachy has had a DRONE detector for months. It had a little drone icon, a page explaining Remote ID, and a decoder that could tell you where the pilot was standing. It had never once spotted a real drone. Somebody pointed a drone spoofer at it from a metre away, got nothing, and filed a bug (thank you, rrahmani). They were right, and it was worse than they thought. Squachy has been staring at the sky with his eyes shut. They're open now.

<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.24.0/docs/look-up.gif" width="480" alt="The DRONE page with a decoded aircraft: its ID, a quad, its position and height, and the operator's position -- where the pilot is standing. Then the LOG with a grey IGNORED tag on one row, and the time zone card showing SE ASIA, S AFRICA and KOREA with the right local time."></p>

**Why he never saw one.** A drone's Remote ID broadcast over Bluetooth is one small packet with its ID crammed into the "service data" part, and it fills the whole thing. Squachy was checking a different part, the list of services a device offers, which a real drone has no room left to send. So every real drone went straight past him. He looks in the right place now. The WiFi version, where drones tuck their ID into their WiFi beacons, was never checked at all. It is now, and the drone's serial number becomes its name in the log. One limit stays: the chip in these boards can't hear the newer Bluetooth 5 long-range broadcasts, and no update can change that.

**Flock-You's signatures.** The Flock-You project (colonelpanichacks, MIT licence) keeps the best list going of how Flock cameras give themselves away, from people out in the field and from a Flock camera's own firmware. Squachy borrowed it, with thanks. That's 20 more WiFi prefixes, a camera network called just "Flock", Flock's own Bluetooth service, all of the Raven gunshot detector's Bluetooth services (including the two that hand out its GPS position), and a Flock battery pack that names itself with a bare serial number. The prefixes belong to chip makers whose parts are in plenty of other gadgets, so they're low confidence, like the ones before. One prefix was left out on purpose: it's Samsung's, and it would have called every Samsung TV in the neighbourhood a police camera.

**Ignored devices wear a tag.** Tell Squachy to ignore something and it used to vanish into a list you couldn't see. The only way to check was to tap IGNORE again and read which message came back. Ignored devices now carry a grey IGNORED tag in the log, and the button says UN-IGNORE, lit up, when a device is already on the list.

**Eighteen more time zones.** The zone list was very American with a side of Europe. It now covers SE Asia, Singapore, Korea, the Gulf, Pakistan, Bangladesh, west, south and east Africa, Turkey, Israel, Mexico, Colombia, Chile, Argentina, Queensland, central Australia and Darwin. They run west to east when you tap through them. The web flasher picks yours from your browser. While we were in there it stopped putting South Africa an hour out all year, and stopped giving Algeria, Tunisia and Brisbane a summer time they don't have.

**Two new boards, in beta.** The Freenove ESP32-S3 Display 2.8" (thanks, greasy-electronics) and the Elecrow CrowPanel Advance 7.0 (thanks, DH5DAX) are on the flasher. Both were built and tested by the people who own them. The CrowPanel is a 7" screen, so Squachy is drawn twice the size, on purpose, and it can chirp its buzzer for a device it hasn't seen before if you ask it to.

### The actually-useful part

**Added**
- Remote ID over WiFi: beacons carrying the ASD-STAN vendor element (FA:0B:BC, type 0x0D) are logged as DRONE, named by the serial in their message pack.
- Flock-You's Flock signatures: 20 WiFi prefixes (LOW), an exact "Flock" SSID, the Flock accessory GATT service, the full Raven range 0x3100-0x3500, and a ten-digit serial name (LOW). Pages for the new labels in MORE INFO.
- Ignored devices show an IGNORED tag on their LOG row (IGN on narrow screens). IGNORE toggles to UN-IGNORE on LOG and on the raw scan.
- 18 time zones: MEXICO, COLOMBIA, CHILE, ARGENTINA, W AFRICA, S AFRICA, E AFRICA, ISRAEL, TURKEY, GULF, PAKISTAN, BANGLADESH, SE ASIA, SINGAPORE, KOREA, QUEENSLAND, AUS CENTRAL, DARWIN.
- Freenove ESP32-S3 Display 2.8" (FNK0104B) and Elecrow CrowPanel Advance 7.0, both BETA, on the web flasher.
- The watch-list alert logs each tap on the console, and whether it was REMOVE or a close.

**Changed**
- Tapping through time zones goes west to east around the world, not in the order they were added.
- The DRONE page says Remote ID is heard over Bluetooth and in WiFi beacons.
- The web flasher's zone guess covers the new zones.

**Fixed**
- Bluetooth Remote ID was matched only in the advert's service UUID list, which a real drone's advert never carries, so no real drone was ever detected.
- The web flasher set South Africa to EU CENTRAL (an hour out all year), and Algeria, Tunisia and Brisbane to zones with a summer time they don't observe.
